standard_prerequisites: The length of a coherent module at a point of a locally Noetherian algebraic space and the support of a coherent module, together with the compatibility of both notions with etale base change to a scheme

The algebra criterion identifying the generic points of the support of a finite module over a Noetherian local ring with the points where the support is the maximal ideal, and finiteness of the module over such a ring
For the decent case: the lifting of specialisations along an etale morphism between spaces and the fact that the underlying spaces of schemes and of decent spaces are sober
core_obligations: Work with an etale morphism from a scheme to the space and the pullback of the coherent module, which is coherent on a locally Noetherian scheme and has finite stalk at the chosen point

Use that the support of the pulled back module is closed and that its stalk at the point is the pullback of the support, so that the point is a generic point of a component of that support exactly when the support of the stalk is the maximal ideal

Read off the equivalence of the three conditions from the algebra criterion on the support of a finite module over the local ring, thereby also proving that the choice of the etale chart is immaterial

In the decent case, compare supports under the etale chart, lift specialisations from the space to the chart and push them down, and use soberness of both spaces to conclude that being a generic point of the support of the module is equivalent to being one after pullback
Record the parenthetical equivalence of decentness and quasi-separatedness used in the last step
proof_roadmap: Pull the module back along an etale chart and translate the generic point condition into a statement about the support of the stalk
Apply the algebra criterion to obtain the equivalence of the three conditions independently of the chart
In the decent case use specialisation lifting and soberness to compare generic points of the support before and after the chart
difficulty_reason: The counted conclusion is the characterisation of the points of finite nonzero length as the generic points of the support of a coherent module at source lines 558-579, label lemma-length-finite, whose proof occupies source lines 581-623. The first half is a translation: coherence, support and length are compatible with an etale chart, and the condition that the point be a generic point of a component of the support becomes the condition that the support of the stalk be the maximal ideal, at which point an algebra criterion for finite modules over a Noetherian local ring settles the equivalence of the three conditions and shows the choice of chart is immaterial. The second half is genuinely topological: for a decent space one must compare, along the chart, which specialisations lift and which descend, and then invoke soberness of both underlying spaces to identify the generic points of the support with those of the pulled back support. The counted statement records neither the chart translation nor the specialisation argument.
